references.text: Joshua 13:21 mentions the same five Midianite kings (Evi, Rekem, Sur, Hur, and Reba) who were killed by the Israelites, confirming that they were vassals under Sihon.
Balaam son of Beor was summoned by Balak to curse Israel. Here in Numbers 31:8 he meets his final fate by the sword.
The verse explains why Balaam was killed: he gave advice that led Israel into sin at Peor.
God commanded Israel to attack the Midianites because of their treachery at Peor, which is now carried out in Numbers 31:8.
Joshua 13:22 confirms that Balaam son of Beor, the diviner, was killed with the sword by the people of Israel.
Peter's letter refers to Balaam's way as an example of error and greed, pointing to his history.
Jude mentions Balaam's error as a warning, referring to his deeds.
Revelation mentions Balaam's teaching, which led Israel into sin through idolatry and sexual immorality.
